bead.title: Isolate embedded Fjord storage namespace
bead.description: PROBLEM: Fjord state is not explicitly proven to live in a namespace separate from pqueue's queue storage, and topic/group state isolation is only implied by config values. ROOT CAUSE: `crates/pqueue-server/src/lib.rs:141-208` builds the embedded surface and exposes `namespace_root`, `offset_store`, and `group_coordinator`, while `crates/pqueue-server/src/lib.rs:287-316` configures the embedded broker with memory-only storage backends and `crates/pqueue-server/src/lib.rs:1110-1111` registers topics at startup without a regression that asserts the namespace boundary. PROPOSED FIX: keep fjord log, offset, and consumer-group state under the embedded namespace root, verify tenant-prefixed topic registration against that root, and add a regression that proves the broker state cannot bleed into pqueue storage. NON-SCOPE: implementing a second Kafka broker, reopening ADR-005 queue-data-plane consumer semantics, or restoring the superseded heimq target.
bead.acceptance:
1. `TestEmbeddedFjordSurfaceUsesDedicatedNamespaceRoot` proves the embedded broker builds its own namespace root instead of sharing pqueue storage.
2. `TestKafkaSurfaceKeepsConsumerGroupStateTenantScoped` proves topic and consumer-group state stay tenant-scoped inside the embedded surface.
3. `go test ./... -run 'TestEmbeddedFjordSurfaceUsesDedicatedNamespaceRoot|TestKafkaSurfaceKeepsConsumerGroupStateTenantScoped'`
4. `lefthook run pre-commit`
5. `lefthook run pre-push`
